name: Vitamin D3
why_needed: Despite being a tropical country with abundant sunlight, indoor lifestyles, dark skin pigmentation (more melanin = less UVB absorption), air pollution (blocks UVB), and vegetarian diets (few dietary D3 sources) cause rampant Vitamin D deficiency across all age groups and socioeconomic strata in India.
when_to_take: With the largest fat-containing meal of the day (D3 is fat-soluble; absorption increases ~50% with fat). Lunch or dinner for most Indians. Morning or afternoon preferred.
forms: Cholecalciferol (D3)
Ergocalciferol (D2) - less effective
contraindications: Hypercalcemia (elevated blood calcium)
Granulomatous diseases (sarcoidosis, tuberculosis) - can cause excessive conversion to active form
Kidney disease - altered metabolism; physician supervision needed
Excessive doses (>4000 IU/day long-term without monitoring) can cause toxicity: hypercalcemia, kidney stones, soft tissue calcification
Take with Vitamin K2 (MK-7) if supplementing >2000 IU/day to direct calcium to bones
who_should_take: Virtually every Indian adult without 20-30 min midday sun on bare arms/legs
Women (especially those wearing full coverage clothing)

research.author: Aparna P et al.
research.finding: Vitamin D deficiency widespread across India

research.author: Ritu G & Gupta A
research.finding: 70-100% of Indians across all demographics are Vitamin D deficient

name: Vitamin B12
why_needed: Predominantly vegetarian/lacto-vegetarian Indian diet causes widespread B12 deficiency. B12 is found almost exclusively in animal products, and dairy alone is often insufficient. Vegans face near-universal deficiency without supplementation. Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia, peripheral neuropathy, cognitive decline, fatigue, elevated homocysteine, and infertility.
when_to_take: Morning, on empty stomach or with breakfast. B12 is water-soluble; no fat needed. Morning helps with energy levels throughout the day.
forms: Methylcobalamin - active form, better retained, preferred
Cyanocobalamin - synthetic, cheaper, well-studied, requires conversion
Hydroxocobalamin - injection form for severe deficiency
Sublingual tablets may have slightly better absorption
contraindications: Extremely safe even at high doses (water-soluble; excess excreted)
Rare allergic reactions to cyanocobalamin
Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy - may worsen (very rare genetic condition)
Very high doses (>5000 mcg/day) - some concern about acne in susceptible individuals
who_should_take: People on metformin (diabetes drug depletes B12)

brands_india.name: Carbamide Forte
brands_india.product: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg + B1, B6, Folic Acid, 100 tablets

research.author: Yajnik CS et al.
research.finding: B12 and folate concentrations during pregnancy affect insulin resistance in offspring

research.author: Refsum H et al.
research.finding: 47-75% of Indian adults have low B12 levels (<200 pg/mL)

name: Vitamin C
indian_deficiency_pct: Low (subclinical insufficiency exists in some populations)
why_needed: Deficiency is less widespread than D3/B12 due to dietary availability (amla, guava, citrus, bell peppers), but subclinical insufficiency exists in malnourished populations and those with poor fruit/vegetable intake. Useful as immune booster, antioxidant, and collagen synthesis aid.

dosage.during_illness: 1000-2000 mg/day in divided doses (may reduce cold duration by ~8%)

when_to_take: With meals (reduces GI upset at higher doses). Morning or any time.
forms: Ascorbic Acid
Sodium Ascorbate (buffered)
Ester-C
contraindications: Doses >2000 mg/day: diarrhea, nausea, stomach cramps, kidney stones (oxalate) in susceptible individuals
Hemochromatosis (iron overload) - Vitamin C increases iron absorption; avoid high doses
G6PD deficiency - very high IV doses can cause hemolysis (oral at normal doses is safe)
History of calcium oxalate kidney stones - keep doses under 1000 mg/day
who_should_take: Those recovering from surgery or wounds (collagen synthesis)
Iron-deficient individuals (enhances non-heme iron absorption - take together)

brands_india.name: Amla (natural alternative)
brands_india.product: Indian gooseberry - 1 amla = ~600-800 mg Vitamin C

name: Vitamin E
indian_deficiency_pct: Low (dietary intake often adequate through cooking oils, nuts, seeds)
why_needed: Dietary intake is often adequate through cooking oils (sunflower, safflower, mustard), nuts, and seeds. Supplementation is mainly useful for skin health and as antioxidant support.
forms: Alpha-tocopherol (natural d-alpha preferred over synthetic dl-alpha)
contraindications: Blood thinning: >400 IU/day can increase bleeding risk. Avoid with anticoagulants (warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel)
Meta-analysis caution: Miller et al. (2005) suggested high-dose >400 IU/day may increase all-cause mortality (debated). Stick to <400 IU/day
Pre-surgery: Stop 2 weeks before elective surgery
who_should_take: Those with poor dietary fat intake

research.author: Miller et al.
research.finding: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day) may increase all-cause mortality (debated)

name: Zinc
why_needed: Approximately 25-30% of Indian adults have zinc deficiency, higher in vegetarian populations due to phytates in grains/legumes inhibiting zinc absorption. Consequences include impaired immunity, poor wound healing, hair loss, low testosterone in men, and taste/smell disturbances.

dosage.during_cold: 75 mg/day in divided doses for 5-7 days only (zinc lozenges)
dosage.upper_limit: 40 mg/day (chronic intake above this causes copper depletion)

when_to_take: On an empty stomach for best absorption (but causes nausea in some - take with small meal if needed). Do NOT take with calcium, iron, or copper supplements at same time. Do NOT take with high-phytate meals (dal/roti/rice). Best taken 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals.
forms: Zinc Picolinate - highest absorption (~20% more bioavailable)
Zinc Glycinate/Bisglycinate - well-absorbed, gentle on stomach
Zinc Citrate - good absorption
Zinc Gluconate - commonly available, decent absorption
Zinc Sulfate - cheapest, can cause nausea; adequate if tolerated
Zinc Oxide - poorly absorbed; avoid for supplementation
contraindications: Copper depletion: Chronic >40 mg/day depletes copper. Supplement copper (1-2 mg) if taking zinc long-term
Reduces absorption of tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics (space 2 hours apart)
who_should_take: Vegetarians/vegans (phytate-rich diet reduces zinc absorption by 30-50%)

research.author: Wessells KR & Brown KH
research.finding: Approximately 25-30% of Indian adults have zinc deficiency, higher in vegetarian populations

name: Magnesium
why_needed: 50-80% of Indians do not meet the RDA for magnesium. Dietary surveys (NNMB data) show median intake of 200-250 mg/day against RDA of 310-420 mg. Causes include refined grain consumption (milling removes ~80% of magnesium), low nut/seed intake, and soil depletion. Consequences: muscle cramps, poor sleep, anxiety, migraines, insulin resistance, poor bone density.

dosage.upper_limit: 350 mg/day from supplements only (higher doses can cause diarrhea)

when_to_take: Evening/before bed for sleep support (glycinate or threonate). With meals to reduce GI side effects. Split doses if >200 mg (absorption saturates). Separate from calcium, zinc, iron supplements by 2 hours.
forms: Magnesium Glycinate/Bisglycinate - Sleep, anxiety, general use; high bioavailability, gentle on stomach
Magnesium Threonate (Magtein) - Cognitive function, brain health; crosses blood-brain barrier
Magnesium Taurate - Heart health, blood pressure; good bioavailability
Magnesium Citrate - Constipation relief, general use; mild laxative effect
Magnesium Malate - Muscle pain, energy, fibromyalgia; good bioavailability
Magnesium Oxide - Cheapest; laxative; poor bioavailability (~4%); avoid
Magnesium L-Threonate - Neurological support; excellent for brain
contraindications: Kidney disease - cannot excrete excess magnesium; risk of hypermagnesemia. Avoid without physician supervision
High doses cause osmotic diarrhea (especially citrate and oxide forms)
Can interact with bisphosphonates, antibiotics (tetracyclines, quinolones) - space 2 hours
who_should_take: People with muscle cramps, poor sleep, anxiety, migraines
Athletes and heavy exercisers (lost in sweat)
People on PPIs or diuretics (deplete magnesium)

brands_india.name: Carbamide Forte
brands_india.product: Magnesium Glycinate (1743 mg, 240 mg elemental), 60 tablets

name: Iron
why_needed: India has among the highest anemia burden globally. ~50% of Indian women (15-49 years), ~25% of men, ~40% of children under 5 are anemic, with iron deficiency being the primary cause (NFHS-5). Do NOT supplement iron unless deficiency is confirmed by blood test - excess iron is dangerous.

dosage.upper_limit: Do NOT supplement without confirmed deficiency

when_to_take: Empty stomach, 1 hour before meals for best absorption. With Vitamin C (200-500 mg) to enhance absorption by 2-3x. Never with tea, coffee, calcium, dairy, or whole grains (tannins, calcium, phytates inhibit absorption by 40-60%). Alternate-day dosing may improve absorption due to hepcidin regulation.
forms: Ferrous bisglycinate - best absorbed, least GI side effects; preferred
Ferrous sulfate - cheap, widely prescribed, causes constipation/nausea
Ferrous fumarate - moderate; common in India
Carbonyl iron - slow release, fewer side effects
contraindications: Do NOT supplement without confirmed deficiency (serum ferritin <30 ng/mL, or hemoglobin <12 g/dL in women, <13 g/dL in men)
Iron overload causes oxidative stress, liver damage, heart damage
Hemochromatosis (genetic iron overload)
Iron supplements are a leading cause of poisoning death in children - store safely
GI side effects: constipation, nausea, black stools (harmless)
Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, tetracyclines, quinolones, levodopa
who_should_take: ONLY if blood test confirms deficiency
Pregnant women (routine supplementation recommended by WHO)
Vegetarians (non-heme iron from plants is less bioavailable)

brands_india.name: Carbamide Forte
brands_india.product: Iron Bisglycinate 60 mg + Vitamin C, 60 tablets

brands_india.name: HealthKart HK Vitals
brands_india.product: Iron + Folic Acid + Vitamin C, 60 tablets

research.author: NFHS-5
research.journal: National Family Health Survey, Government of India
research.finding: ~50% of Indian women, ~25% of men, ~40% of children under 5 are anemic

research.author: Moretti et al.
research.finding: Alternate-day iron dosing may improve absorption due to hepcidin regulation

name: Calcium
indian_deficiency_pct: Widespread - average intake 300-400 mg/day against RDA of 600-1000 mg
why_needed: Average Indian dietary calcium intake is only 300-400 mg/day (NNMB data), against an RDA of 600-1000 mg. Consequences include osteopenia, osteoporosis (especially post-menopausal women), and fracture risk.
when_to_take: Calcium Carbonate: with meals (needs stomach acid). Calcium Citrate: any time (acid-independent). Split doses (max 500 mg per dose). Separate from iron and zinc by 2 hours. Take with Vitamin D3 (critical for absorption). Consider adding Vitamin K2 (MK-7).
forms: Calcium Citrate - absorbed with or without food; better for those on PPIs/low stomach acid; preferred
Calcium Carbonate - cheapest, must be taken with food, 40% elemental calcium; can cause gas/constipation
Calcium Hydroxyapatite - derived from bone; contains phosphorus; well-absorbed
contraindications: Kidney stones (calcium oxalate type) - dietary calcium reduces risk, but supplements may increase it; take with meals to bind oxalate
Hypercalcemia, hyperparathyroidism - do not supplement
Cardiovascular concern - some meta-analyses suggest calcium supplements may increase CV risk; keep <1500 mg/day from supplements
Drug interactions: reduces absorption of thyroid medications, bisphosphonates, tetracyclines - space 2-4 hours

brands_india.name: Tata 1mg Calcium
brands_india.product: Calcium Citrate Malate + D3 + K2, 60 tablets

name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids
indian_deficiency_pct: Widespread - omega-6:omega-3 ratio often 15-20:1 instead of ideal 2-4:1
why_needed: Indian diets are typically very high in omega-6 (from sunflower, soybean, groundnut oil) and low in omega-3, creating an unfavorable ratio. Fish consumption is limited in many regions (especially North/West India). Vegetarian omega-3 sources provide ALA but conversion to EPA/DHA is very low (5-10% for EPA, <1% for DHA).

dosage.vegetarian_ala: 1-2 tablespoons flaxseed oil (~7g ALA) or ground flaxseeds
dosage.algae_based: 250-500 mg combined EPA+DHA from algal oil

when_to_take: With a fat-containing meal (improves absorption significantly). Can be taken any time of day. If taking high doses (>2g), split into 2 doses with meals.
forms: ALA (Alpha-Linolenic Acid) - plant-based from flaxseeds, chia, walnuts; poor conversion to EPA/DHA
EPA (Eicosapentaenoic Acid) - from fish or algae; anti-inflammatory, mood support
DHA (Docosahexaenoic Acid) - from fish or algae; brain, eye, heart health
Algae-based DHA/EPA - best vegetarian option for preformed EPA/DHA
contraindications: Blood thinning: High doses (>3g/day) may increase bleeding time. Caution with anticoagulants
Fish burps: Enteric-coated capsules reduce this; freeze capsules before taking
Fish allergy: Use algae-based alternatives
Surgery: Stop high-dose supplementation 1-2 weeks before surgery
who_should_take: Most Indians (due to poor omega-3:omega-6 ratio)
Those not consuming fish 2-3 times per week
Pregnant women (DHA for fetal brain development)

brands_india.product: Fish Oil 1000 mg (180 EPA/120 DHA), 60 capsules

brands_india.product: Triple Strength 1250 mg (560 EPA/400 DHA), 60 capsules

name: Ashwagandha
why_needed: One of the most well-researched Ayurvedic herbs with multiple randomized controlled trials. Shown to reduce cortisol by 27.9%, increase testosterone by ~15%, improve muscle strength, reduce anxiety significantly, improve sleep quality, and normalize thyroid hormones in subclinical hypothyroidism.

dosage.ksm_66_root_extract: 300-600 mg/day (typically 300 mg twice daily); standardized to >5% withanolides
dosage.sensoril_root_leaf_extract: 125-250 mg/day; more potent per mg, more calming
dosage.cycle_recommendation: 8-12 weeks on, 2-4 weeks off (traditional Ayurvedic practice)

when_to_take: For stress/anxiety: morning and evening, with meals. For sleep: 300-600 mg, 30-60 minutes before bed. For testosterone/muscle: morning and post-workout or evening.
forms: KSM-66 (root extract) - most studied
Sensoril (root + leaf extract) - more potent per mg, more calming
Raw powder (Churna) - traditional use, less concentrated
contraindications: Pregnancy - AVOID (may have abortifacient properties)
Autoimmune conditions (lupus, RA, Hashimoto's, MS) - stimulates immune system, may worsen flares
Hyperthyroidism or properly treated hypothyroidism - can elevate thyroid hormones
Surgery - stop 2 weeks before (may enhance anesthesia effects)
May lower blood sugar and blood pressure - caution with diabetes/BP medications
Liver concerns - rare case reports of liver injury (use reputable brands)
Nightshade family - may cause GI upset in nightshade-sensitive people
who_should_take: Adults experiencing chronic stress, anxiety, or poor sleep
Athletes seeking improved recovery and strength
People with subclinical hypothyroidism (under medical supervision)

research.author: Chandrasekhar et al.
research.finding: 300 mg KSM-66 twice daily reduced cortisol by 27.9% and perceived stress significantly vs placebo over 60 days

research.author: Lopresti et al.
research.finding: 300 mg KSM-66 twice daily increased testosterone by ~15% and improved sperm quality

research.author: Wankhede et al.
research.finding: Improved muscle strength, recovery, gained more muscle mass, lost more body fat

research.author: Pratte et al.
research.finding: 5 RCTs showed significant anxiolytic effects

research.author: Langade et al.
research.finding: 300 mg twice daily improved sleep quality significantly in healthy and insomnia patients

research.author: Sharma et al.
research.finding: Normalized thyroid hormones in subclinical hypothyroid patients (600 mg/day for 8 weeks)

name: Shilajit
why_needed: Contains fulvic acid and dibenzo-alpha-pyrones which may enhance mitochondrial energy production. Shown to increase total testosterone by 20.45% and free testosterone by 19.14% in healthy men aged 45-55 over 90 days. Improves sperm count and motility in infertile men.

dosage.traditional: Pea-sized amount (~300 mg) dissolved in warm milk or water

when_to_take: Morning on empty stomach (traditional recommendation) with warm water or milk. Can also take in the evening.
forms: Purified Shilajit resin
Capsule/tablet (standardized extract)
Traditional resin dissolved in warm milk or water
contraindications: Purity is critical: Raw/unprocessed Shilajit may contain heavy metals, mycotoxins, free radicals. ONLY use purified/processed forms from reputable brands
Hemochromatosis/iron overload - Shilajit is rich in iron
Gout/high uric acid - may increase uric acid in some individuals
Pregnancy/breastfeeding - insufficient safety data; avoid
Not studied adequately in children
who_should_take: Those seeking energy and vitality improvement
Those interested in traditional Ayurvedic wellness

research.author: Pandit et al.
research.finding: Purified Shilajit 250 mg twice daily increased total testosterone by 20.45% and free testosterone by 19.14% in healthy men over 90 days

research.author: Biswas et al.
research.finding: Improved sperm count, motility, and testosterone in infertile men

research.author: Surapaneni et al.
research.finding: Fulvic acid and dibenzo-alpha-pyrones may enhance mitochondrial energy production

name: Brahmi
why_needed: One of the most evidence-backed nootropic herbs. Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs showed Bacopa significantly improves attention, cognitive processing, and working memory. Active compounds (bacosides) have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and acetylcholinesterase inhibitory properties. Requires 4-12 weeks of consistent use for noticeable cognitive improvement.
when_to_take: With meals (fat-containing, as bacosides are fat-soluble). Morning or afternoon for cognitive benefits during the day. Effects are not immediate - requires 4-12 weeks of consistent use.
forms: Standardized extract (45-50% bacosides)
BacoMind extract (patented full-spectrum)
Raw powder (traditional)
contraindications: GI upset - most common side effect (nausea, cramps, bloating, diarrhea); take with food
May increase acetylcholine - caution with cholinergic drugs or acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
Thyroid - some evidence Bacopa may increase T4 levels; caution in hyperthyroidism
Pregnancy/breastfeeding - insufficient data; avoid
May have mild sedative effect - may enhance effects of CNS depressants
Fertility - some low-quality animal studies suggest high doses may reduce sperm motility (not confirmed in humans)
who_should_take: Students and professionals seeking cognitive enhancement
Those experiencing brain fog or difficulty concentrating

research.author: Pase et al.
research.finding: Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs: Bacopa significantly improved attention, cognitive processing, and working memory

research.author: Stringer et al.
research.finding: 300 mg/day for 12 weeks improved memory acquisition and retention

research.author: Roodenrys et al.
research.finding: 300 mg/day improved speed of visual information processing, learning rate, and memory consolidation

name: Probiotics
indian_deficiency_pct: N/A (supplementary; traditional Indian diet includes natural probiotics)
why_needed: Growing awareness of gut health in India. Traditional Indian diet includes natural probiotics: curd/dahi (Lactobacillus), idli/dosa batter (fermented), kanji, pickles, buttermilk. Supplementation useful after antibiotics, for IBS, and for those with poor dietary diversity.
when_to_take: On empty stomach or 30 minutes before meals (less acid exposure = more bacteria survive). Some evidence that taking with a meal containing fat improves survival. Any consistent timing is fine.
forms: Capsules (multi-strain)
Probiotic drinks (Yakult)
Sachets (prescription - Darolac, VSL#3)
Natural sources: curd/dahi, buttermilk, idli/dosa, kanji, pickles
contraindications: Generally very safe
Immunocompromised patients - risk of bacteremia/fungemia (rare but documented)
Short bowel syndrome, central venous catheters - increased risk
SIBO (Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth) - may worsen symptoms in some people
Histamine intolerance - some strains produce histamine. Choose L. rhamnosus, B. longum that degrade histamine
who_should_take: People with IBS or digestive issues
People experiencing bloating or irregular digestion

brands_india.name: Yakult
brands_india.product: Probiotic drink (L. casei Shirota, 6.5 billion CFU)

name: Whey Protein / Plant Protein
indian_deficiency_pct: >70% of Indians are protein-deficient by recommended standards
why_needed: Average protein intake in Indian vegetarian diets is 0.6-0.8 g/kg, often below recommended 0.8-1.0 g/kg for sedentary adults, and well below 1.4-2.0 g/kg for active individuals. ICMR data shows >70% of Indians are protein-deficient by recommended standards.

dosage.sedentary_adult: 0.8 g/kg body weight total daily (0-1 scoops supplement)

when_to_take: Post-workout (within 2 hours) for optimal muscle protein synthesis. Morning to break overnight fast. Before bed (casein) for slow-release overnight recovery. Total daily protein matters more than timing.

forms.best_for: Vegan; combine with pea for completeness

contraindications: Kidney disease - high protein intake may accelerate decline in those with pre-existing kidney disease (no evidence it harms healthy kidneys)
Lactose intolerance - use whey isolate (minimal lactose) or plant protein
Milk allergy - use plant protein
Contamination risk in India - many brands found to contain heavy metals, amino spiking, or undeclared ingredients. Buy from verified sources; check for Informed Sport/FSSAI certification
who_should_take: Anyone not meeting daily protein targets through diet
Those aiming for muscle building or fat loss

research.author: Antonio et al.
research.finding: No evidence high protein intake harms healthy kidneys

research.author: Messina
research.finding: Soy estrogen concern is overblown at moderate intake (2-3 servings/day is fine)
